name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
summary: A hip-hinge barbell exercise emphasizing eccentric loading of the hamstrings and glutes while maintaining a neutral spine.

setup: Stand tall holding a loaded barbell with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Position your feet hip-width apart with toes pointing forward or slightly outward.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down, brace your core, and unlock your knees slightly.
steps: Hinge at the hips by pushing your pelvis straight backward while keeping a soft, fixed bend in your knees.
Lower the barbell in a straight line close to your thighs and shins until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Reverse the motion once your hips stop traveling backward, driving your hips forward to return to the upright starting position.
Finish by squeezing your glutes at the top without hyperextending your lower back.
instructions.breathing: Inhale and brace your core at the top before hinging; exhale as you lock out your hips near the top of the ascent.
cues: Push your hips to the wall behind you
Keep the bar glued to your legs
Maintain a soft knee bend without squatting

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lumbar spine to reach lower to the floor.
common_faults.correction: Stop descending when your hips stop moving backward; range of motion is determined by hamstring flexibility, not touching the floor.

common_faults.fault: Squatting the weight down by bending the knees excessively.
common_faults.correction: Keep your knees softly unlocked at a fixed angle and focus entirely on pushing your hips backward.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the barbell to drift away from the legs.
common_faults.correction: Engage your lats to keep the bar skimming along your thighs and shins throughout the lift.

precautions: Do not sacrifice neutral spinal alignment to gain extra depth.
Use lifting straps if grip fatigue compromises form.
